title_en: Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Yongxiu County People's Government, Jiangxi Province, and the Office of the Leading Group for Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management of Yongxiu County — dispute over mining rights
ruling_gist_en: 1. The act of a party publishing an open auction promotion document on a website is essentially an invitation to offer issued to an unspecified public regarding the open auction. When the offeree enters into a contractual relationship with the offeror, and the parties dispute the content of the contract as agreed, such invitation to offer may have evidentiary effect in interpreting the contract.
keywords_en: civil; mining rights dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Jiangxi Province; Sichuan Province; legal person; state organ; Contract Law; General Principles of Civil Law; application of the principle of change of circumstances; effect of invitation to offer; whether the purpose of the contract can be achieved; reversal of judgment; mining rights auction; drought leading to water level decline; difficulty in contract performance; principle of fairness; mining rights dispute (Leading Group Office)
full_text_en:
Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Yongxiu County People's Government of Jiangxi Province, and the Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Work Leading Group Office of Yongxiu County — dispute over mining rights

[Ruling Summary]

I. The act of a party publishing an open auction promotion document on a website is essentially an invitation for offer made to unspecified persons in society regarding the open auction. If a contract is established between the offeree and the party, and a dispute arises over the content agreed in the contract, such invitation for offer may serve as evidence for the interpretation of the contract.

II. The principle of fairness is a fundamental principle that parties shall follow when concluding and performing civil contracts. The Interpretation II of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, in accordance with the provisions on the principle of fairness in the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, establishes the principle of change of circumstances during the performance of a contract. Article 26 of such Interpretation provides: "After the formation of a contract, if there is a significant change in the objective circumstances that was unforeseeable by the parties at the time of concluding the contract, which is not caused by force majeure and does not constitute a commercial risk, and if continuing to perform the contract is manifestly unfair to one party or makes it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract, and a party requests the people's court to modify or rescind the contract, the people's court shall, in accordance with the principle of fairness and based on the actual circumstances of the case, determine whether to modify or rescind the contract." Accordingly, if the purpose of the contract cannot be achieved due to unforeseeable changes in the natural environment, and continuing to perform the contract would inevitably result in one party obtaining all the contract gains while the other party bears all the investment losses, the people's court shall support the request of the aggrieved party to modify certain terms of the contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 91

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 108, Science and Technology Wealth Center, Gaoxin Incubation Park, South Extension of Gaoxin District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Wei, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wan Biwen, lawyer of Jiangxi Yangzhongyang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Qu Songping, lawyer of Beijing Xinyi Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Yongxiu County People's Government of Jiangxi Province, domiciled at Yongxiu County, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Yaochun, County Head.

Agent ad litem: Luo Aiping, lawyer of Jiangxi Boyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Huang Caitian, lawyer of Jiangxi Boyi Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Work Leading Group Office of Yongxiu County, domiciled at Yongxiu County, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Gong Quanwu, Head of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Baosheng, lawyer of Beijing Jindu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jie, lawyer of Beijing Jindu Law Firm.

The appellant, Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pengwei Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2007) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 rendered by the Jiangxi High People's Court regarding a dispute over mining rights with the respondents, Yongxiu County People's Government of Jiangxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Yongxiu County Government) and the Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Work Leading Group Office of Yongxiu County (hereinafter referred to as the Sand Mining Office). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Judge Zhang Shuming serving as the presiding judge, and Acting Judges Sha Ling and Zhou Lunjun participating in the trial. Zhao Suijun served as the court clerk. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

In 2006, the Yongxiu County Government decided to auction the sand mining rights of four mining areas, namely Areas 5, 6, 7, and 8, in the Poyang Lake waters of Yongxiu County. The Sand Mining Office prepared and published on the website "China Investment Online" the "Promotion Brochure for Sand and Stone Investment Attraction in Yongxiu County (Poyang Lake Sand Mining Development Project)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Promotion Brochure"). The Promotion Brochure stated: "The flood season of Poyang Lake comes early and lasts long, from early April to the end of November each year, with a mining period of up to 200 days; the investment amount is over RMB 110 million, mainly for the purchase of mining rights and taxes; total sales revenue can reach RMB 700 million to 1 billion, with profits of RMB 50 to 70 million." To facilitate investment attraction, staff of the Sand Mining Office compiled the "2006 Feasibility Report on Sand Mining in Yongxiu Mining Area, Poyang Lake, Jiangxi Province" (hereinafter referred to as the "Feasibility Report"), which provided a detailed analysis and budget for the investment prospects of sand mining rights, including operational profit models, equipment investment, personnel allocation, and benefits: calculated based on daily mining of 260 vessels, each carrying 1,500 tons, at RMB 8 per ton, the daily sales revenue from pump vessels could reach RMB 3.12 million. The investor, receiving a 30% commission, could earn RMB 936,000 per day. For a full mining season calculated at 180 days, total revenue could reach RMB 168.48 million. Costs included the mining rights price of RMB 110 million, plus costs for speedboats, vessel rentals, fuel, personnel wages, living expenses, interest, maritime safety supervision, industrial and commercial fees, etc., totaling approximately RMB 118.324 million (based on a 6-month mining period). The profit was RMB 50.156 million. In the risk section, the Feasibility Report pointed out that sand mining involved policy risks, market risks, and natural risks. "Natural risk: if a low-water year occurs, it will have a significant impact on the mining period. However, 1998 was a high-water year in the Yangtze River basin. Eight years have passed since 1998. According to general patterns, this year should also be a high-water year. Even if it is not a high-water year, based on the normal water level of Poyang Lake, mining for 6 months (180 days) from early May to the end of October should be no problem." The "Assessment Report on the Three Mining Areas 6, 7, and 8 of Poyang Lake (2006)" provided by the Sand Mining Office to Zhang Wei, Chairman of Pengwei Company, also stated: "The normal operating time of the mining areas is from mid-May to mid-November this year, with a full year period of 6 months. For a conservative investment assessment, subtracting factors such as weather, it is assumed that the normal operating time is 4 months (120 days)."

On April 17, 2006, the Jiangxi Provincial Water Resources Department issued the reply document Gan Shui Zheng Fa Zi (2006) No. 24, the main contents of which were: "In principle, approve the auction plan for the sand mining rights in some waters of Poyang Lake, Yongxiu County, for 2006. The auction mining period is from May 1, 2006, to December 31, 2006, with a control of 38 sand mining vessels and an annual controlled total mining volume of 23.2 million tons." The appendix to the reply stated: "For Mining Area 6 of Poyang Lake, Yongxiu County: controlled pump vessels 5, annual controlled mining volume 1.1 million tons; Mining Area 6-1: controlled pump vessels 5, annual controlled mining volume 6 million tons; Mining Area 7: controlled pump vessels 10, annual controlled mining volume 3.3 million tons; Mining Area 7-1: controlled pump vessels 4, annual controlled mining volume 5 million tons; Mining Area 8: controlled pump vessels 2, annual controlled mining volume 500,000 tons; Mining Area 8-1: controlled pump vessels 2, annual controlled mining volume 1.5 million tons; a total ban on mining for more than four months per year."

The Sand Mining Office entrusted Shandong Silver Star Auction Co., Ltd. to handle the auction of the sand mining rights. The "List of Auction Items" and "Special Provisions for the Auction" prepared by the parties stated: "The starting price for the sand mining rights of Mining Areas 6, 7, and 8 in Poyang Lake, Yongxiu County, is RMB 40.68 million; the buyer shall bear the work expenses of RMB 252,000 for the mining areas, calculated at RMB 1,000 per vessel per month based on the approved number of sand mining vessels; taxes and fees of RMB 35.5 million, including state taxes payable, river sand mining management fees, and mineral resource compensation fees." On April 26, 2006, Pengwei Company bid RMB 46.78 million to win the sand mining rights for Mining Areas 6, 7, and 8 in the Poyang Lake waters of Yongxiu County. Subsequently, Pengwei Company paid a total of RMB 82.28 million to the Yongxiu County Non-tax Revenue Administration Bureau, which issued fee receipts for the corresponding amounts, with the fee item names all being "Mining Area Auction Payment." On May 10, 2006, the Sand Mining Office and Pengwei Company formally signed the "Contract for the Granting of Sand Mining Rights for Mining Areas 6, 7, and 8 in Poyang Lake, Yongxiu County" (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights"), which stipulated: "1. The term of the sand mining rights is from the date of signing this contract to December 31, 2006, subject to flood control requirements; the number of sand mining vessels is 28 (each with power within 4,000 kw); the annual controlled mining volume is 17.4 million tons; 2. The auction transaction amount is RMB 82.28 million (including taxes and fees); 10. The term of the sand mining rights for the mining areas stipulated in this contract is based on the effective minable period for the current year as approved by the superior competent authority; the actual minable period is subject to the water level of the year when it is no longer sufficient for sand mining vessels to operate."

From July 2006 onwards, Jiangxi Province experienced persistent high temperature and drought weather, with less rainfall. The Yangtze River section in Jiangxi saw an unusually low water level for the same period, and a large amount of water from Poyang Lake flowed into the Yangtze River, causing the water level to drop sharply, reaching a low water level rarely seen since the early 1970s. On August 18, 2006, due to the low water level of Poyang Lake making it difficult for sand transport vessels to enter the mining areas, Pengwei Company was forced to stop sand mining. In response, Pengwei Company wrote to the Sand Mining Office requesting solutions to issues such as the shortened mining time and insufficient sand sources. According to a certificate from the Yongxiu County Port and Shipping Administration Office, the office collected cargo port dues from sand mining vessels operating in Mining Areas 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the Yongxiu waters of Poyang Lake each day from 6:00 to 18:00 during 2006. A total of RMB 8,757,740 was collected, with 7,935 valid fee receipts, indicating a sand volume of 8,757,740 tons and 7,935 vessel trips. Accordingly, the average cargo capacity per sand transport vessel for Mining Areas 5, 6, 7, and 8 in the Yongxiu waters of Poyang Lake was 1,103.6849 tons. Based on Pengwei Company's admission that it transported sand for a total of 20,900 vessel trips, it can be inferred that the mining volume was 23,067,015 tons. According to archival data from the Jiangxi Provincial Hydrological Bureau, the average daily water level at the Xingzi Station of the Hukou Waterway on August 18, 2006, was 13.05 meters, a level that generally appeared after mid-to-late October since 1970. According to the Sand Mining Office and Pengwei Company, the price of sand in Poyang Lake in 2006 ranged between RMB 6 and 8 per ton.

The court of first instance also found: The Sand Mining Office is a directly affiliated public institution of Yongxiu County Government, with the purpose and business scope of: being responsible for publicizing relevant national laws, regulations, and policies, coordinating the relations among all parties involved in sand mining, supervising sand mining, maintaining normal order in sand mining, and with funding sources from fiscal appropriations. According to the "2006 Implementation Measures for Sand Mining Management in the Yongxiu Jurisdiction of Poyang Lake," the sand mining management work leading group was composed of the main leaders of relevant departments and units of the Yongxiu County Party Committee and Government, with the Sand Mining Office established under the leading group to handle the daily work of sand mining, and its work expenses were arranged by the Yongxiu County Finance Bureau. After the dispute in this case arose, the sand mining rights for Mining Areas 5, 6, and 7 in the Yongxiu waters of Poyang Lake for 2007 were acquired by auction by Yongxiu County Water Resources and Hydropower Construction Engineering Company, which signed the "Agreement on the Management of River Sand Mining in the Yongxiu Waters of Poyang Lake" with the Yongxiu County Water Affairs Bureau, stipulating that the mining period "is in principle from the signing of this agreement to December 31, 2007, with the actual minable period subject to the water level of the year when it is no longer sufficient for sand mining vessels to operate. At the same time, it shall satisfy flood control requirements and unforeseen related policies such as national key construction requirements. All risks arising from objective reasons such as water levels causing inability to produce shall be borne by Yongxiu County Water Resources and Hydropower Construction Engineering Company." The annual controlled mining volume for the sand mining rights acquired by Yongxiu County Water Resources and Hydropower Construction Engineering Company was 23.8 million tons, with a contract price of RMB 60.16 million, including river sand resource fees of RMB 19.04 million. The company commenced mining on June 20, 2007, and ceased operations on October 10, 2007.

In August 2007, Pengwei Company filed a civil lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: to rescind the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" signed with the Sand Mining Office; the Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government to compensate for the missing 135 days of mining period in accordance with the contract and provide all tax and fee invoices; if the Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government could not make up the mining period, to refund the auction transaction price overpaid by Pengwei Company of RMB 47.27 million (including taxes and fees); and to bear the litigation costs. During the first instance trial, Pengwei Company withdrew the claim for compensation for the missing 135 days of mining period.

The court of first instance held that: The Sand Mining Office is a functional institution established by the Yongxiu County Government responsible for the daily management of sand mining. It auctioned the sand mining rights under the authorization of the Yongxiu County Government, and the legal consequences of such act shall be borne by the Yongxiu County Government. The "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" signed between the Sand Mining Office and Pengwei Company reflected the true intentions of the parties, its contents complied with the restrictions on the number of sand mining pump vessels, annual controlled mining volume, and mining ban period stipulated in the reply document of the Jiangxi Provincial Water Resources Department, and did not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws or administrative regulations, and thus should be deemed legal and valid. Pursuant to Article 1 of the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" regarding the annual controlled mining volume and Article 10 regarding the actual minable period, Pengwei Company's sand mining rights were subject to dual restrictions of both mining volume and mining period. That is, when the water level of the Yongxiu waters of Poyang Lake was sufficient for sand mining operations, the upper limit of Pengwei Company's mining volume was 17.4 million tons. Once this volume was reached, Pengwei Company should stop mining, and the contract would be performed. When the water level of the Yongxiu waters of Poyang Lake naturally dropped due to seasonal and climatic changes, making it impossible for sand mining pump vessels and transport vessels to operate, even if Pengwei Company had not yet reached the mining volume of 17.4 million tons, it could only stop mining, and the rights and obligations under the contract would terminate. Since the hydrological conditions of Poyang Lake vary each year, it was impossible to accurately predict the specific time when mining operations would become impossible due to falling water levels at the time of concluding the contract. Therefore, the expression of the mining period in the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" was relatively general, with Article 10 stating that "the actual minable period is subject to the water level of the year when it is no longer sufficient for sand mining vessels to operate." Thus, the court did not accept Pengwei Company's argument that this clause indicated its acquired sand mining rights were only limited by the mining period and not by the mining volume. Based on the available evidence, it could be inferred that as of August 18, 2006, when sand mining operations ceased, Pengwei Company's sand mining volume was 23,067,015 tons, which had exceeded the annual controlled mining volume of 17.4 million tons stipulated in the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights." Therefore, the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" had been performed before August 18, 2006, upon reaching the contractually agreed mining volume. The subsequent lack of water for mining, whether or not it constituted force majeure, could not constitute a reason for rescinding the contract. Accordingly, Pengwei Company's claim for rescission of the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" based on force majeure causing part of the sand mining rights not to be realized was not supported. Moreover, even if, as Pengwei Company argued, the income from the 17.4 million tons of sand mining rights did not constitute reasonable consideration for the contract price of RMB 82.28 million, because its bid and auction were for the purpose of obtaining a sand mining right for a certain period, and after obtaining the sand mining right, in order to obtain economic benefits, it would inevitably violate the restrictions in the Jiangxi Provincial Water Resources Department's reply document by exceeding the mining volume. The purpose of Pengwei Company's contract was unlawful. Under the theory of unjust enrichment due to unlawful purpose in civil law, when an unlawful contract purpose cannot be realized, the law should not protect a claim for the return of part of the contract price already paid. Regarding Pengwei Company's claim for the provision of tax invoices, since the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" did not stipulate this, it was not within the scope of this case. After discussion by the judicial committee, the court, in accordance with Article 8 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the judgment: Dismiss all of Pengwei Company's claims. The case acceptance fee was RMB 306,350, to be borne by Pengwei Company.

Pengwei Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing:

(1) The restriction on sand mining volume in the "Contract for Granting Sand Mining Rights" signed by both parties did not reflect their true intentions. The open auction "Promotion Brochure" published by the Sand Mining Office on the "China Investment Online" website stated that the mining period could be as long as 200 days, with total sales revenue reaching RMB 700 million to 1 billion. Calculated accordingly, the annual sand mining volume could reach over 100 million tons. After Pengwei Company won the bid, when signing the contract with the Sand Mining Office, it immediately raised objections to the volume restriction clause added to the contract. The main leaders of the Yongxiu County Party Committee and Government explained that adding the volume restriction to the contract was "to cope with the inspection by the Provincial Water Resources Department" and promised the appellant that "there would be no actual restriction" on the sand mining volume. If the mining volume were restricted to 17.4 million tons, the total sales revenue would be less than RMB 140 million. Calculated at a gross profit of RMB 2 per ton, the gross income of the mining rights holder would be only RMB 34.8 million. If the project were carried out, the mining rights holder would not only fail to make a profit but would lose RMB 48 million. The first instance finding that Pengwei Company actually mined 23,067,000 tons of sand was insufficiently evidenced and inconsistent with the facts.

(2) During the performance of the contract, a once-in-a-century severe drought occurred, reducing the effective mining period by 135 days compared to the contractually agreed period, making the purpose of the contract unattainable. Pengwei Company had acquired sand mining rights, but in the actual performance of the contract, Pengwei Company did not obtain the corresponding mineral products as per the contract. The Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government did not lose the corresponding amount of mineral resources but obtained the full contract price according to the contract. This created an unfair situation in contract performance, contrary to the basic principles of the Contract Law.

(3) Given that the Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government could not extend the mining period to allow the appellant to continue mining, and modifying the contract to remedy the losses was no longer possible, Pengwei Company could only request the Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government to refund part of the contract price exceeding the reasonable consideration. Based on the ratio of Pengwei Company's actual exercise period of sand mining rights to the contractually agreed mining period of 235 days, Pengwei Company requested the return of RMB 47.27 million. According to the contract, the taxes and fees of RMB 33.5 million paid by Pengwei Company were included in the total contract price and had been collected by the Sand Mining Office on behalf. However, the Sand Mining Office had not paid these fees. The Sand Mining Office and Yongxiu County Government were obliged to return the overpaid portion to Pengwei Company. Pengwei Company's claims at first instance were lawful and reasonable. It requested the second instance to set aside the original judgment and amend the judgment to support its first instance claims.

Appellee Yongxiu County Government and the Sand Mining Office responded in defense: (1) The Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract is truthful, lawful, and valid. The 17.4 million tons is the administrative licensing limit on annual extraction imposed by the superior competent administrative department. The Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract explicitly stipulates the annual controlled extraction volume as 17.4 million tons. Pengwei Company signed and affixed its official seal to the contract, indicating its acknowledgment of and no objection to the contract. Pengwei Company's denial of this stipulation by citing the Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report on the grounds that it does not represent the true intent of both parties is not credible. The Promotion Brochure and Feasibility Report are not integral parts of the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract and are not legally binding on the contracting parties. Pengwei Company claims that county leaders promised unlimited extraction but has adduced no evidence to prove which leader made such a promise, or when and where. (2) Pengwei Company's argument that during the performance of the contract, an unprecedented severe drought occurred once in a century, reducing the effective extraction period by 135 days from the contractually agreed period, thereby causing unfairness in actual performance, cannot stand. First, the provisions of the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract regarding "the term of the sand mining rights shall be from the date of signing this contract to December 31, 2006" and "the actual extractable period of the sand mining rights shall be determined by the water level of the year when it is no longer suitable for mining vessel operations" are stipulations concerning the contract performance period and the actual extractable period. The contract does not stipulate a mandatory extraction period of 235 days. Since there is no such stipulation of a 235-day mandatory extraction period, there can be no reduction of 135 days in the effective extraction period. Sand mining in Poyang Lake is a special industry dependent on water level operations. The duration of extraction depends on the water level of Poyang Lake. The natural phenomenon of high and low water levels in Poyang Lake determines that sand mining cannot continue beyond November of the year. The hydrological data provided by Pengwei Company also fully confirms this fact. (3) Sand mining in Poyang Lake is a high-risk, high-reward special industry with significant temporal and seasonal characteristics, inherently containing substantial commercial risk. Pengwei Company's participation in the bidding for the mining rights indicates its knowledge and acceptance of this risk. Therefore, the occurrence of low water levels after August 18 rendering extraction impossible is a commercial risk that Pengwei Company must bear on its own. Pengwei Company's claim of unfair performance results based on a change of circumstances has no legal basis. As of August 18, Pengwei Company had extracted 23,067,015 tons, already exceeding the annual controlled extraction volume of 17.4 million tons, thereby realizing the contract's purpose. The subsequent low water levels preventing extraction could not cause unfairness in the contract's performance results. Of the RMB 82.28 million paid by Pengwei Company, RMB 46.78 million was the bid price for the sand mining rights determined through auction proceedings, which does not involve the issue of change of circumstances. The RMB 35.5 million was taxes and fees levied by the administrative department based on the annual controlled extraction volume of 17.4 million tons under an administrative legal relationship, which also does not involve the issue of change of circumstances. Pengwei Company's request for the return of RMB 47.27 million, calculated by proportionally converting the actual extraction period to the 235-day extraction period beyond the reasonable consideration, is legally unfounded. It requests the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

This Court confirms the facts found at the first instance in the second instance trial.

Opinion of the Court: The Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract entered into by the Sand Mining Office and Pengwei Company through a public auction represents the true intent of the parties. Its content does not violate prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations and should be deemed lawful and valid.

The Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract stipulates: the term of the sand mining rights runs from the date of signing this contract to December 31, 2006, with an annual controlled extraction volume of 17.4 million tons; the term of the sand mining rights for the extraction area stipulated in this contract is the effective extractable period for the current year as approved by the superior competent department, and the actual extractable period shall be determined by the water level of the year when it is no longer suitable for mining vessel operations. Regarding these stipulations, Pengwei Company contends that the 17.4 million ton extraction limit in the contract does not reflect the true intent of Pengwei Company and the Sand Mining Office. It alleges that during the signing of the contract, a key leader of Yongxiu County Government explained that the inclusion of the extraction limit was to cope with the inspection by the Provincial Water Resources Department, and promised that the actual extraction volume would not be restricted. In the first instance trial of this case, Pengwei Company submitted as evidence the public auction Promotion Brochure published by the Sand Mining Office on its website and the Feasibility Report compiled by the Sand Mining Office staff to support its claim. Yongxiu County Government and the Sand Mining Office argue that the annual controlled extraction volume of 17.4 million tons is an administrative licensing limit on annual extraction by the superior competent administrative department. Pengwei Company signed and sealed the contract only after having no objection to the 17.4 million ton stipulation. This stipulation is clear, and the validity of the contract cannot be negated by the Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report written by an individual.

Regarding this, this Court holds: The public auction Promotion Brochure published by the Sand Mining Office on the "China Investment Online" website constitutes an invitation to offer issued to unspecified persons concerning the public auction of sand mining rights. When an offeree establishes a contractual relationship with the offeror and the parties dispute the content of the contract's stipulations, this invitation to offer may serve as evidence for the interpretation of the contract. The Feasibility Report compiled by the Sand Mining Office staff, consistent in content with the Promotion Brochure, concretizes and interprets the offer and can be used as evidence in this case. Both the Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report, using an example of a total investment of RMB 110 million for extraction areas 5, 6, 7, and 8, promoted the acquisition of sand mining rights through auction. Calculated based on the shorter extraction period of 180 days in the Feasibility Report, at RMB 8 per ton of lake sand, with the investor receiving a 30% royalty, extracting 17.4 million tons of lake sand would yield a profit of RMB 41.76 million. That is, if the contract is interpreted as a limited-volume contract of 17.4 million tons, Pengwei Company's return on investment would be only RMB 41.76 million, which is clearly disproportionate to the total payment of RMB 82.28 million to the Sand Mining Office for the sand mining rights price and taxes and fees. Therefore, this Court supports Pengwei Company's claim that the 17.4 million ton extraction limit did not represent the true intent of both parties, and the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract is a contract limited by time but not by volume. During the actual performance of the contract, the Sand Mining Office, as the regulatory authority for sand mining, did not supervise or restrict Pengwei Company's extraction volume. In the first and second instance proceedings, it also failed to provide evidence of the specific extraction figures of Pengwei Company, the specific time when extraction reached 17.4 million tons, or the management measures taken thereafter. This indicates that the Sand Mining Office was not genuinely concerned about the 17.4 million ton extraction limit, which indirectly proves that the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract was not a genuine limited-volume contract.

In the first instance proceedings, the Sand Mining Office adduced evidence that Pengwei Company transported sand in 20,900 vessel trips, which Pengwei Company acknowledged. The first instance court estimated Pengwei Company's actual extraction volume at 23,067,015 tons based on the average tonnage of sand-carrying vessels. Pengwei Company argued that using the average tonnage of large vessels was unscientific but failed to provide relevant evidence of actual extraction volume. The first instance court's determination is appropriate and should be upheld. Calculated according to the investment return method set out in the Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report, based on Pengwei Company's actual extraction of 23,067,015 tons, its actual revenue is approximately RMB 55.34 million. Compared to its payment of RMB 82.28 million, it remains in a loss position.

Based on the facts found at the first instance, Pengwei Company commenced sand mining operations after signing the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract on May 10, 2006, and ceased operations on August 18, 2006, extracting for a total of 100 days. The reason for the cessation was: after July 2006, Jiangxi Province experienced sustained high temperatures and drought, with below-average rainfall. The Yangtze River section in Jiangxi experienced a rare low water level for that period. A large volume of Poyang Lake water flowed into the Yangtze River, causing a sharp drop in water levels, reaching a rare low water level not seen since the early 1970s. The excessively low water level of Poyang Lake made it difficult for sand-carrying vessels to enter the extraction area, forcing Pengwei Company to cease operations. According to archival records from the Jiangxi Provincial Hydrological Bureau, on August 18, 2006, the daily average water level at the Xingzi Station of the Hukou Waterway was 13.05 meters, a level that since 1970 typically appeared after mid-to-late October. Both parties have no dispute over these facts. Therefore, it can be determined that due to the rare low water level in Poyang Lake not seen in 36 years, Pengwei Company's sand extraction ended prematurely. This natural disaster has a direct causal relationship with Pengwei Company's losses. Both Pengwei Company and the Sand Mining Office have no dispute on this point.

The principle of fairness is a fundamental principle that parties should follow when entering into and performing civil contracts. Article 26 of this Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "After a contract is established, if a material change occurs in the objective circumstances that the parties could not have foreseen at the time of entering into the contract, which is not caused by force majeure and does not constitute commercial risk, and continuing to perform the contract is manifestly unfair to one party or makes it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract, and a party requests the people's court to modify or rescind the contract, the people's court shall determine whether to modify or rescind the contract in accordance with the principle of fairness and in light of the actual circumstances of the case." In this case, although the sand mining rights in the Yongxiu section of Poyang Lake acquired by Pengwei Company were obtained through bidding, bidding was merely the specific method adopted by Pengwei Company and the Sand Mining Office to conclude the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract. The contractual conduct between the parties remains subject to the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. During the performance of the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract in this case, Pengwei Company encountered a rare low water level in Poyang Lake not seen in 36 years, which prevented sand mining vessels from operating in the extraction area, caused the early termination of sand extraction, failed to achieve the contract purpose stipulated in the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract, and resulted in huge losses. This objective circumstance was unforeseeable by both Pengwei Company and the Sand Mining Office at the time of signing the contract. Pengwei Company's losses are not caused by commercial risk. Under these circumstances, continuing to perform the contract strictly according to its terms would inevitably result in the Sand Mining Office obtaining all contractual benefits while Pengwei Company bears all investment losses, which is unfair to Pengwei Company and contradicts the fundamental principles of contract law. Pengwei Company's request for the Sand Mining Office to refund part of the contract price is essentially a request to modify certain terms of the Sand Mining Rights Transfer Contract, which is consistent with the Contract Law and the aforementioned judicial interpretation of this Court. This Court supports this request.

Based on the calculation method of investment return set out in the Sand Mining Office's Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report, Pengwei Company's revenue from extracting 23,067,015 tons of lake sand is approximately RMB 55.34 million, with an actual extraction period of 100 days, i.e., daily revenue of RMB 553,400. At this rate, to recover costs and offset its paid RMB 82.28 million in sand mining rights price and taxes and fees, Pengwei Company would need to extract for at least 149 days. Additionally, based on facts found at the first instance, on August 18, 2006, due to the excessively low water level in Poyang Lake making it difficult for sand-carrying vessels to enter the extraction area, Pengwei Company was forced to cease operations. According to archival records from the Jiangxi Provincial Hydrological Bureau, at this time, the daily average water level at the Xingzi Station of the Hukou Waterway of Poyang Lake was 13.05 meters, a level that since 1970 typically appeared after mid-to-late October. Based on this, it can be inferred that had the extremely low water level not occurred since 1970, Pengwei Company's sand extraction time would have been around 160 days. The extraction periods determined by both the above two calculation methods are essentially consistent with the promotion of the extraction period in the Sand Mining Office's Promotion Brochure and the Feasibility Report. In accordance with the principle of fairness in sharing losses, and considering the actual circumstances of this case, this Court determines that the Sand Mining Office should compensate Pengwei Company for a total of 30 days of sand extraction in extraction areas 6, 7, and 8. Given that sand mining in Poyang Lake is highly seasonal and obtaining sand mining rights requires relatively strict administrative licensing procedures, and the parties were unable to reach agreement on compensation for the extraction period in the second instance, the Sand Mining Office should refund part of the sand mining rights transfer price as an alternative to compensation for the extraction period.

Pengwei Company's first instance request for the Sand Mining Office to refund the overpaid auction price of RMB 47.27 million actually comprises two components: a request for the Sand Mining Office to refund part of the sand mining rights transfer price and a request for a refund of overpaid taxes and fees. Taxpayers paying taxes and fees to administrative organs is not a civil act between equal parties and is not suitable for trial as a civil case. Therefore, this case does not address Pengwei Company's claim for a refund of part of the sand mining taxes and fees. Pengwei Company may pursue this claim with the relevant administrative authorities or file a separate administrative lawsuit. Of the RMB 82.28 million auction price paid by Pengwei Company, the sand mining rights transfer price was RMB 46.78 million. Calculated based on an extraction period of 130 days, the daily price is RMB 359,800. Pengwei Company actually extracted for 30 fewer days. Therefore, the Sand Mining Office should refund Pengwei Company RMB 10,795,400 for the sand mining rights transfer price.

The Sand Mining Office is a directly affiliated institution of Yongxiu County Government and the daily working body of the Yongxiu County Sand Mining Management Leading Group. The Sand Mining Management Leading Group comprises key leaders from relevant departments of the Yongxiu County Party Committee and County Government. The Sand Mining Office is funded by fiscal appropriations and lacks the capacity to independently bear civil liability. Therefore, Yongxiu County Government should bear the civil liability in this case jointly with the Sand Mining Office.

In summary, the first instance judgment correctly found the facts but erroneously applied the law and improperly handled the substance. This Court corrects this. Some of Pengwei Company's appeal claims have factual and legal basis and are supported by this Court. Pursuant to Article 5 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 26 of this Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2007) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 of the Jiangxi High People's Court is set aside;

2. The People's Government of Yongxiu County, Jiangxi Province and the Office of the Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Leading Group of Yongxiu County shall refund Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. RMB 10,795,400 for the sand mining rights transfer price within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment;

3. The other claims of Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. are rejected.

The first instance court acceptance fee of RMB 306,350 shall be borne jointly by the People's Government of Yongxiu County, Jiangxi Province and the Office of the Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Leading Group of Yongxiu County in the amount of RMB 183,810, and by Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 122,540. The second instance court acceptance fee of RMB 306,350 shall be borne jointly by the People's Government of Yongxiu County, Jiangxi Province and the Office of the Poyang Lake Sand Mining Management Leading Group of Yongxiu County in the amount of RMB 183,810, and by Chengdu Pengwei Industrial Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 122,540.

This judgment is final.
